subject: Post-call recap & evaluation plan — throughput vs quality for Finlynx
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finlynx.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & proposed eval — throughput vs quality

Hi Emily — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick written recap so we have a shared plan and scope for the short eval we discussed.

Summary of customer goals (from call):
- Latency SLO: p95 < 250ms for interactive search/rewrite flow
- Throughput: ~120 qps peak (batched), typical 30–40 qps
- Quality target: no more than ~2–3% drop in Rouge/BLEU-like score on your internal test set vs baseline fp16
- Procurement constraint: prefer hosted evaluation but may need Dedicated for longer-running runs

Our recommended test matrix (short eval):
1) Baseline: redwood-instruct-65b fp16 (hosted) — accuracy baseline
2) AWQ quantized model (8-bit activation-aware) on same architecture — measured latency/throughput + quality delta
3) GPTQ (8-bit GPTQ) variant — compare quality/throughput tradeoffs
4) FP8 experimental run (if you want to push throughput) — only if quality delta above threshold is acceptable

Deliverables we propose:
- 1-page summary of model fit with metrics (latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, quality scores)
- Full run logs and KV cache behavior notes
- Prompt set and evaluation harness (attached)
- Cost/throughput estimate for Dedicated capacity if you want to lock in throughput

Attachments: finlynx_prompt_set_v1.txt (prompt examples + test queries), throughput_tradeoffs.xlsx (sample numbers from internal runs), awq_vs_gptq-runplan.md (step-by-step plan).

Next steps / ask:
- Can you confirm the 2–3% quality tolerance and whether we should prioritize latency or throughput if tradeoffs arise?
- If yes, we can schedule a 48–72 hour run on hosted infra (small credit) — need your green light and preferred start window.

If you want, we can also run a very small A/B on your sample dataset through Dedicated capacity (costed) to prove p95 under load.

Thanks — I’ll block a short follow-up for Wed to finalize scope unless you want to pick a start date now.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finlynx.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@finlynx.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed eval — throughput vs quality

Thanks Jordan — this is great and matches my notes. A couple quick clarifications: 

- Quality tolerance: the 2–3% number is our soft gate — engineering will accept up to 3% across our rewrite task, but product team will want a qualitative check for hallucinations/edge-case degradations.
- Latency vs throughput: prefer to optimize for p95 latency first; throughput is secondary but we need the option to scale later.
- Compliance: can you attach your SOC2 or point me to where the security team can pull evidence?

We’d like the hosted 48–72 hour run to start as soon as next Monday (10/19) if that works. Also, please include an estimated run credit or cost for the hosted eval (and a ballpark for Dedicated reservation if we want to try that).

Emily Zhao
Director of Product | Finlynx
emily.zhao@finlynx.ai

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finlynx.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Post-call recap & proposed eval — throughput vs quality

Lauren / Marcus — forwarding Emily's confirmation. Please see below and advise:

Ask summary from customer: start hosted 48–72h eval w/ test matrix (baseline fp16, AWQ, GPTQ, optional FP8) starting 2026-10-19. Priority: p95 latency. Quality tolerance: up to 3%, but product will perform qualitative checks. They need SOC2 link for compliance.

Questions for infra team: 
- Can we run the AWQ and GPTQ variants back-to-back within a single 72h hosted window at the required concurrency (simulate 30–120 qps, burst patterns)?
- Rough credit estimate: based on our previous runs, 72h of mixed-quant runs at this scale = ~ $1,800–2,400 in hosted credits (range depends on AWQ speedups). Please confirm.
- If we need Dedicated trial for a single day to validate p95 under load, what is the minimal reservation we can offer as a short burst? Include cost/billing note for sales.

Proposed internal plan: Marcus to spin the run harness and AWQ/GPTQ build; Lauren to draft the brief and cost estimate; I’ll send SOC2 link and customer-facing run plan doc.

Marcus / Lauren — can you confirm timeline today so I can reply and lock 10/19 start?

Jordan

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finlynx.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed eval — throughput vs quality

Emily — quick follow-up with the links and a slightly more concrete schedule. Thanks for confirming the tolerance.

Planned schedule (tentative):
- 10/19 09:00 PDT: start baseline fp16 run (24h)
- 10/20 09:00 PDT: AWQ run (24h) + immediate metric aggregation
- 10/21 09:00 PDT: GPTQ run (24h) + final aggregation and 1-page summary

Estimated hosted eval credit: $2,100 (midpoint estimate). If we find p95 slipping under the AWQ variant, we’ll switch that test to a Dedicated 1-day burst (we can provide a discounted reserved day) — ballpark reserved-day price for that capacity is $2,400/day.

SOC2: https://vault.redwood.com/compliance/soc2-report-2025.pdf
Benchmark / run plan: https://drive.redwood.com/benchmark/finlynx-throughput-20261012 (contains prompt set and eval harness)

If that schedule looks fine I’ll lock and provision the hosted cluster. We’ll also surface any AWQ/GPTQ-specific prompt-sensitivity notes if we see regressions on edge cases (we’ll flag any >1.5% regression immediately).

Thanks — Jordan
